summary: Same beat-locked light organ — a 4-band colour group tiled across the strip, redrawn on every 2 Hz beat and decaying between beats, alternating between a crisp 'calm' regime and an arcing 'busy' regime — but the port runs that slow regime alternation on a 40 s cycle instead of the original's ~60 s, places its dark bands differently (never producing the original's wide black gaps), and adds white sparkle the original does not have.
observations: Alive on both sides, no compile or runtime errors; both report wantsSensors true and were fed the identical beat120 synthetic signal on every run.
Neither side exposes any control (probe: '(no settable controls)' on both) — control surfaces match.

Core mechanism matches: on every beat both sides pick a group of 4 colour slots and tile it repeatedly across the 60 px strip, then hold the colours while brightness decays exponentially until the next beat. At 20/40/80 fps both re-trigger every 0.50 s (measured from motion-series peak spacing on runs fps20/fps40/fps80): orig gaps 0.50 s x39, port 0.50 s x44.

Both sides have TWO slow regimes, and the port reproduces both: a 'calm' regime where the band geometry is frozen for the whole beat (crisp rectangular blocks in the waterfall) and a 'busy' regime where the band widths shrink as the beat decays, so the tiling contracts and the waterfall fills with curved arcs (orig at --skip 70, port at --skip 22 and --skip 100 look like the same effect).

REGIME CYCLE PERIOD DIFFERS. Over a 300 s / 20 fps run (label long300), 5-second-block mean motion shows the original entering its busy regime at t≈60, 120, 180 and 245 s — period ~60-65 s, busy stretch ~35 s (motion ~30 vs ~11 calm). The port enters at t≈20, 60, 100, 140, 180, 220, 260 s — period exactly 40 s, busy stretch ~20 s (motion ~47 vs ~16 calm). So the port cycles through its busy phase about 1.5x too often.

DARK-BAND PLACEMENT DIFFERS. Census of 240 beats over 120 s (--dump one frame per beat, label dump-120s): in the calm regime the original's 179 sampled beats are ALWAYS 4 equal-width slots (group period exactly 4, 8, 12 or 16 px, i.e. slot width 1-4 px), with either 1 dark slot or 2 dark slots that are always ADJACENT (giving black runs of 2w, up to 8 px). The port's 106 calm beats include 45 with the two dark slots ALTERNATING with the lit ones (signatures C4+K4+C4+K4 x14, C2+K2+C2+K2 x13, C1+K1+C1+K1 x11, C3+K3+C3+K3 x7) — a layout the original produces 0 times in 240 beats.

Consequence, measured on the default 60 px rig over 120 beats: the original's black run-widths are 1,2,3,4,6,8 px (6 and 8 px runs are the merged double-dark slots, 111 occurrences); the port's black runs never exceed 4 px and are 1 px in 648 of 1069 cases. The port therefore reads as a denser, gap-poorer strip.

In the busy regime the 1 px dark slot IS genuine original behaviour (orig busy signatures C4+K1+C4+C4 x30, K5+C4+C1 x21), so that feature is right — but the port's busy-regime lit slots are usually 5 px wide (C5+K1+C5+K1 x28, C5+K1+C4+C4 x27) where the original's are 4 px.

WHITE SPARKLE. On the exact beat-attack frame the original whitens 1.8% of pixels and the port 12.6% (40 beat-attack frames dumped, label dump-attack). Mid-beat (+0.05 s and +0.35 s offsets, 480 frames) the original has 0.00% whitish pixels in BOTH regimes while the port holds 0.94% — the port's white specks persist through the decay, the original's exist only on the attack frame.

Colour otherwise matches well: hue histograms over 120 beats both peak hard in the 0-30 deg red bin (orig 127, port 148) with a secondary blue cluster (orig 210-240 deg x68, port 240-270 deg x45) and the rest spread thinly. Mean channel levels over 20 s at 20 fps: orig R76/G31/B47, port R77/G44/B39 — the port is slightly greener and slightly less blue.

Overall brightness at the harness default is close: 20 s at 20 fps gives orig meanBrightness avg 51.2 (min 29, max 114), port 53.4 (min 19, max 143). The port's per-beat attack is brighter (143 vs 114 peak) and then decays a little harder.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING. The original's decay envelope is frame-stepped, the port's is time-based. Same 20 s window: orig mean brightness 51 @20 fps, 42 @40 fps, 27 @80 fps (at 80 fps it goes 'volatile', min 0, 119 zero-motion frames — it nearly dies between beats); port holds 53 / 59 / 59 and stays 'steady'. Measured on one beat at t=5 s, brightness falls 73->38 in 0.5 s at 20 fps but 109->10 at 80 fps on the original, while the port falls 107->33 / 107->43 at the same two rates.

Knock-on effect below 20 fps: at 10 fps the original re-triggers only every 1.5-3.0 s (missing most beats) while the port still fires every 0.50 s; at 5 fps the original fires every 1.8-6.0 s and the port every 0.8-1.0 s. At 20 fps and above the two agree exactly, so this only bites at survey rates.

Steady state is not a problem for either side — the original is 'steady' at every rate tested and the port is 'steady'/'decaying' only in the sense of its beat envelope; a --skip 100 --seconds 20 window still shows both fully alive. But at t=100-120 s the two look clearly different because the port is in its busy regime and the original is in its calm one (port: arcs + white specks, motion 47; orig: crisp blocks, motion 11).
Seed-independent: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give statistically identical runs on both sides (orig mean 50-51 / motion 11, port mean 54-55 / motion 16-17).
With --sensors off BOTH sides render pure black with zero motion — identical (and graceful) degradation with dead sensors.
feedback: The slow regime alternation is the biggest fixable divergence: the original spends ~35 s in the 'busy' (band-width-contracting, arcing) regime and ~25 s in the 'calm' (frozen-geometry, crisp-block) regime, a ~60-65 s cycle; the port runs 20 s busy / 20 s calm, a 40 s cycle. Slow whatever drives that alternation by about 1.5x and lengthen the busy phase relative to the calm one.

In the calm regime the original's 4 slots are ALWAYS equal width and its dark slots are always contiguous: you see either one dark slot of width w or two adjacent dark slots forming a 2w-wide gap (black runs of 6 and 8 px are common on a 60 px strip). The port instead frequently darkens slots 0 and 2, giving an alternating lit/dark/lit/dark comb with no gap wider than 4 px. Whatever chooses which bands are silent should keep the silent ones adjacent, not interleaved.

The port emits far too much white: 12.6% of pixels whiten on the beat attack versus the original's 1.8%, and the port keeps ~1% white specks alive all the way through the decay while the original has literally none between attacks. Confine the white flash to the attack frame and reduce its extent.
In the busy regime the port's lit bands are 5 px wide where the original's are 4 px (with the same 1 px dark slot on both) — the port's contracted group period is one pixel too wide.

The original's brightness decay is frame-stepped (it decays a fixed fraction per rendered frame, so it dims dramatically as frame rate rises: mean brightness 51 at 20 fps, 42 at 40 fps, 27 at 80 fps), while the port's decay is time-based and holds ~55-59 at every rate. On real hardware running at hundreds of fps the original would look much snappier and darker than the port. Match the original's per-frame decay if fidelity at the device's real frame rate matters.

Minor colour nudge: the port's mean green is ~44 against the original's ~31 and its mean blue ~39 against ~47 over the same 20 s window — the port's secondary hue cluster sits around 240-270 deg where the original's sits around 210-240 deg.
